To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have measured the peak energy and line shape for 97 L x ray transitions in four elements of the rare earth series, and that we have established an absolute energy calibration for the range from 4 keV through 10 keV with a relative accuracy of 0.1%.

the L x ray emission spectra of praseodymium, neodymium, terbium, and holmium can be modeled by a sum of one to five Voigt functions, and that the peak energy of each of these lines is measured with a median uncertainty of 0.25 eV.
we have measured 97 L x ray emission lines of praseodymium (Pr), neodymium (Nd), terbium (Tb), and holmium (Ho) with a median uncertainty of 0.2 eV on the line peak energies.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the measurement of the absolute energies and emission line profiles of the L x rays from four of the lanthanides, praseodymium through holmium.
the measurement of the x-ray emission spectra of rare earth elements, and in particular the lanthanides.

the development and use of a new generation of cryogenic microcalori- meters for high-resolution x-ray spectrometry and with the application of these instruments to the determination of the absolute energies of x-ray emission lines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new data are the best available for the elements and transitions measured.
these new measurements of lanthanide L x ray emission lines are the best available data for this energy range.
the present work is a significant improvement in the accuracy, scope, and completeness of the available data on lanthanide L x ray emission lines.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

it improves the accuracy and precision of the absolute x ray energy calibration for this spectral range, and it expands the scope of reference data on the line shapes of x rays from the rare earth elements.
the new measurements provide a more accurate and more complete reference for L x ray energies and line shapes of these elements.
it provides the most accurate and complete reference data for L x ray emission lines of the lanthanides.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the L x ray line profiles of the lanthanides are more complex than previously thought, requiring multiple Voigt functions in order to adequately model the observed profiles.
the line shapes for the lanthanide L lines are not well described by single Voigt functions.
the energy resolution of transition edge sensor spectrometers is sufficiently high that the line shapes of the measured lines are not well described by the Voigt profile.
